thread:
leo_sales: Quick sync  prospect (regional fintech) pushed back. They need BYOK with HSM-backed CMKs, mandatory per-day ephemeral KEK rotation, and SIEM-forwarded attestation. Also asked how rotation affects SLA and billing.

anya_se: Short answer: feasible. We have two POC topologies: 1) Hosted + external-KMS-proxy (we call their HSM for wrap/unwrap) or 2) Dedicated in their VPC with customer HSMs peered. Hosted is fastest; Dedicated is best for high qps and predictable latency.

mike_crypto: Rotation semantics: ephemeral KEKs rotated daily is fine. Implementation: generate ephemeral DEKs server-side, wrap with customer CMK via PKCS#11 or cloud-HSM API, store only the wrapped DEK. For attestation, we can log PKCS#11 op IDs and forward signed attestations to their SIEM.

leo_sales: They want explicit numbers: how much latency per wrap/unwrap when proxying to external HSM?

anya_se: Typical added latency 840ms depending on network and HSM vendor. If they require <50ms p95 for request end-to-end and do many wraps inline, we should propose a hybrid cache of wrapped prefixes or move to Dedicated.

tara_ops: For the POC we'll provision a small dedicated cluster to emulate production. Need their HSM endpoint IPs, mTLS certs, and expected concurrency. Ops will also enable dashboards: wrap latency histogram, rpc errors, and socket churn.

leo_sales: Billing: do we charge per-crypto-op or per-token? They asked for a predictable model for budgeting.

mike_crypto: Recommended: base per-token hosted fee + optional HSM-connect add-on priced per-1000 crypto ops for external HSM proxy. Dedicated deals: fixed monthly connector + usage tier for extremely high wrap rates. Also charge a one-time ceremony/onboarding fee and an annual attestation package.

emma_legal: We'll need to prepare a Key Custody FAQ and an appendix in the SOW. Must include: statement that Redwood never has plaintext CMK access, audit log retention, and procedures for emergency key recovery/escrow. If they request dual-custody with third-party escrow, add fee and chain-of-custody terms.

leo_sales: They also asked for an example of the POC runbook and a snippet to show firewall rules. Can someone post a short runbook?

anya_se: Draft runbook snippet:
```
POC runbook (48h)
1. Collect HSM endpoints + mTLS certs from customer (T-3 days)
2. Provision staging pool + wireguard to customer gateway
3. Run connectivity test: pkcs11 list-keys / wrap-unwrap smoke test
4. Start 48h soak, monitor wrap latency and error rates
5. Deliver attestation logs and SIEM webhook snapshot
```
Firewall sample (customer side):
```
allow tcp 203.0.113.10:443 -> 198.51.100.22:8443 (mTLS)
```
I'll flesh this out and attach to the ticket.

tara_ops: Ops checklist: allocate ephemeral certs, schedule maintenance window for jump host, enable tcp keepalive, and set circuit-breaker at 5% wrap error rate to failover to fallback-model.

build-bot: ticket created  sales/POC-1837002468: "fintech BYOK rotation POC". Assignee: anya_se. Due: 72 hours.

leo_sales: One last: rotation window impact on SLA. If they rotate KEKs daily inline, do we need to extend maintenance window or does it cause downtime?

mike_crypto: No downtime expected for rotation if using wrapped DEK model. Rotation is atomic: create new DEK, wrap with CMK, start issuing new tokens, and retire old wrapped DEKs after TTL. Document rollback steps if wrap fails. We'll include a block diagram in the runbook.

emma_legal: I'll draft the appendix and a short answer to their security questionnaire Qs about key custody.

anya_se: I'll produce the pricing slide + runbook draft by EOD tomorrow.

leo_sales: Sweet. I'll schedule the customer meeting for Fri 11am PT and send the draft slides. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
